# Quick Start

Follow these steps to quickly set up ESLint Plugin Boundaries in your project. Then you can explore more advanced configurations to fit your project's needs, starting with [Classification](./classification/classification.md).

## 1. Installation

If you [have not installed them yet](./installation.mdx), install ESLint and ESLint Plugin Boundaries:

```bash
npm install eslint eslint-plugin-boundaries --save-dev
```

## 2. Register the Plugin

Once installed, enable the plugin in your `eslint.config.js` file:

<Tabs>
<TabItem value="JavaScript">

```javascript
import boundaries from "eslint-plugin-boundaries";

export default [
  {
    plugins: {
      boundaries,
    },
  }
];
```

</TabItem>
<TabItem value="TypeScript">

```typescript
import boundaries, { Config } from "eslint-plugin-boundaries";

export default [
  {
    plugins: {
      boundaries,
    },
  } satisfies Config
];
```

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

## 3. Define your Elements

Elements classify a project by the architectural piece each file belongs to. Define them using the [`boundaries/elements` setting](./classification/elements.md).

These patterns determine how each file or dependency is classified. This step is optional on its own — as the [next step](#4-categorize-your-files) explains, you only need to define **at least one** classification layer, elements or files.

:::tip
Read the **[Classification](./classification/classification.md)** section for guidance on how to define the patterns for the elements and files in your project.
:::

<Tabs>
<TabItem value="JavaScript">

<CodeDiff language="javascript">{`
. import boundaries from "eslint-plugin-boundaries";

. export default [
.   {
.     plugins: {
.       boundaries,
.     },
+     settings: {
+       "boundaries/elements": [
+         { type: "helper", pattern: "helpers/*" },
+         { type: "component", pattern: "components/*/*" },
+         { type: "module", pattern: "modules/*" }
+       ],
+     },
.   }
. ];
`}</CodeDiff>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value="TypeScript">

<CodeDiff language="typescript">{`
. import boundaries, { Config, Settings } from "eslint-plugin-boundaries";

. export default [
.   {
.     plugins: {
.       boundaries,
.     },
+     settings: {
+       "boundaries/elements": [
+         { type: "helper", pattern: "helpers/*" },
+         { type: "component", pattern: "components/*/*" },
+         { type: "module", pattern: "modules/*" }
+       ],
+     } satisfies Settings,
.   } satisfies Config
. ];
`}</CodeDiff>

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

:::info
This is only a basic example of configuration. The plugin can also capture path fragments from element paths so you can reuse them in rule policy selectors. Read **[Elements](./classification/elements.md)** to learn the full range of descriptor options.
:::

:::note
Element patterns match **folders** (e.g. `components/*/*`), not individual files. To classify files by kind — tests, styles, stories — use [file descriptors](./classification/files.md) in `boundaries/files`, as shown in the next step.
:::

## 4. Categorize your Files

This step is optional. The plugin needs at least one classification layer to work, so you only have to define **either** [elements](./classification/elements.md) **or** [file](./classification/files.md) descriptors — the previous step is optional too, and defining both is not required.

While elements group files into architectural units (usually folders, such as `components/Button/`), file descriptors classify each file **on its own**, independently of the element it belongs to. They answer the question "what kind of file is this?" — a test, a style, a story — regardless of where it lives. Define them with the [`boundaries/files` setting](./classification/files.md).

<Tabs>
<TabItem value="JavaScript">

<CodeDiff language="javascript">{`
. import boundaries from "eslint-plugin-boundaries";

. export default [
.   {
.     plugins: {
.       boundaries,
.     },
.     settings: {
.       "boundaries/elements": [
.         { type: "helper", pattern: "helpers/*" },
.         { type: "component", pattern: "components/*/*" },
.         { type: "module", pattern: "modules/*" }
.       ],
+       "boundaries/files": [
+         { pattern: "**/*.spec.js", category: "test" },
+         { pattern: "**/*.css", category: "style" }
+       ],
.     },
.   }
. ];
`}</CodeDiff>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value="TypeScript">

<CodeDiff language="typescript">{`
. import boundaries, { Config, Settings } from "eslint-plugin-boundaries";

. export default [
.   {
.     plugins: {
.       boundaries,
.     },
.     settings: {
.       "boundaries/elements": [
.         { type: "helper", pattern: "helpers/*" },
.         { type: "component", pattern: "components/*/*" },
.         { type: "module", pattern: "modules/*" }
.       ],
+       "boundaries/files": [
+         { pattern: "**/*.spec.js", category: "test" },
+         { pattern: "**/*.css", category: "style" }
+       ],
.     } satisfies Settings,
.   } satisfies Config
. ];
`}</CodeDiff>

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

:::info
File categories are independent from elements, so the same file can be element type `component` **and** file category `test` at the same time. Unlike element types, every matching descriptor contributes its category, so a file can carry several at once. Read **[Files](./classification/files.md)** to learn the full range of file descriptor options.
:::

:::note
The rest of this guide keeps these file descriptors so you can see the `file` layer matched in a rule policy. If you skip this optional step, simply omit the `boundaries/files` setting and any rule that targets `file`.
:::

## 5. Apply Predefined Rules

Apply one of the [predefined rule configurations](./settings/config-helpers.md) as a starting point by extending it in your `rules` section.

:::tip
Use `recommended` for existing projects to introduce rules gradually — it allows files outside defined elements. Use `strict` for new projects to require all files to belong to a known element from the start.
:::


<Tabs>
<TabItem value="JavaScript">

<CodeDiff language="javascript">{`
. import boundaries from "eslint-plugin-boundaries";

. export default [
.   {
.     plugins: {
.       boundaries,
.     },
.     settings: {
.       "boundaries/elements": [
.         { type: "helper", pattern: "helpers/*" },
.         { type: "component", pattern: "components/*/*" },
.         { type: "module", pattern: "modules/*" }
.       ],
.       "boundaries/files": [
.         { pattern: "**/*.spec.js", category: "test" },
.         { pattern: "**/*.css", category: "style" }
.       ],
.     },
+     rules: {
+       ...boundaries.configs.recommended.rules,
+     },
.   },
. ];
`}</CodeDiff>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value="TypeScript">

<CodeDiff language="typescript">{`
. import boundaries, { Config, Settings, Rules } from "eslint-plugin-boundaries";

. export default [
.   {
.     plugins: {
.       boundaries,
.     },
.     settings: {
.       "boundaries/elements": [
.         { type: "helper", pattern: "helpers/*" },
.         { type: "component", pattern: "components/*/*" },
.         { type: "module", pattern: "modules/*" }
.       ],
.       "boundaries/files": [
.         { pattern: "**/*.spec.js", category: "test" },
.         { pattern: "**/*.css", category: "style" }
.       ],
.     } satisfies Settings,
+     rules: {
+       ...boundaries.configs.recommended.rules,
+     } satisfies Rules,
.   } satisfies Config
. ];
`}</CodeDiff>

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

## 6. Set Dependencies Rule Policies

Now you can define your own dependency rule policies using the [`boundaries/dependencies` rule](./rules/dependencies.md).

:::tip
Read how to use **[Selectors](./selectors/selectors.md)** to configure your [Rule Policies](./policies/policies.mdx) in detail.
:::

<Tabs>
<TabItem value="JavaScript">

<CodeDiff language="javascript">{`
. import boundaries from "eslint-plugin-boundaries";

. export default [
.  {
.    plugins: {
.      boundaries,
.    },
.    settings: {
.      "boundaries/elements": [
.        { type: "helper", pattern: "helpers/*" },
.        { type: "component", pattern: "components/*/*" },
.        { type: "module", pattern: "modules/*" }
.      ],
.      "boundaries/files": [
.        { pattern: "**/*.spec.js", category: "test" },
.        { pattern: "**/*.css", category: "style" }
.      ],
.    },
.    rules: {
.      ...boundaries.configs.recommended.rules,
+      "boundaries/dependencies": [2, {
+        default: "disallow",
+        policies: [
+          {
+            from: { element: { types: "component" } },
+            allow: { to: { element: { types: "helper" } } }
+          },
+          {
+            from: { element: { types: "module" } },
+            allow: { to: { element: { types: ["component", "helper"] } } }
+          },
+          {
+            // No element may import a test file, whatever element it belongs to
+            disallow: { to: { file: { categories: "test" } } }
+          }
+        ]
+      }]
.    },
.  },
. ];
`}</CodeDiff>

</TabItem>
<TabItem value="TypeScript">

<CodeDiff language="typescript">{`
. import boundaries, { Config, Settings, Rules } from "eslint-plugin-boundaries";

. export default [
.  {
.    plugins: {
.      boundaries,
.    },
.    settings: {
.      "boundaries/elements": [
.        { type: "helper", pattern: "helpers/*" },
.        { type: "component", pattern: "components/*/*" },
.        { type: "module", pattern: "modules/*" }
.      ],
.      "boundaries/files": [
.        { pattern: "**/*.spec.js", category: "test" },
.        { pattern: "**/*.css", category: "style" }
.      ],
.    } satisfies Settings,
.    rules: {
.      ...boundaries.configs.recommended.rules,
+      "boundaries/dependencies": [2, {
+        default: "disallow",
+        policies: [
+          {
+            from: { element: { types: "component" } },
+            allow: { to: { element: { types: "helper" } } }
+          },
+          {
+            from: { element: { types: "module" } },
+            allow: { to: { element: { types: ["component", "helper"] } } }
+          },
+          {
+            // No element may import a test file, whatever element it belongs to
+            disallow: { to: { file: { categories: "test" } } }
+          }
+        ]
+      }]
.    } satisfies Rules,
.  } satisfies Config
. ];
`}</CodeDiff>

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

:::info
You can customize the error messages reported by rule policies using **[message templates](./policies/policies.mdx)**.
:::

## 7. Next Steps

You are all set! Now you can start enforcing architectural boundaries in your project 🎉

From here you can:

- Explore the configuration sections to learn:
  - How to **[Classify Elements and Files](./classification/classification.md)**.
  - How to **[define Selectors to match dependencies](./selectors/selectors.md)**.
  - How to **[define Rule Policies using those Selectors](./policies/policies.mdx)**.
  - How to **[customize Global Settings](./settings/settings.md)**.
- Review the **[Rules section](./rules/rules.md)** to understand all available rules and how to configure them.
- Browse the **[Guides](./guides/monorepo-setup.md)** for task-oriented walkthroughs, such as setting up a monorepo.
